title: RFP-Admin Operations Guide — Run the Platform

lede: The operator's journey: monitor sources, ingest and curate RFPs, push opportunities to customers, release their purchases, and oversee every workflow and agent from one console.
Screenshots are the live admin console. Where a customer's work needs a hand, you shadow-descend into their portal, do the work, and rise back up to ingest more — all as one account.
hero.badge: master_admin holds global access · every action is audited

footer: govwin — RFP Pipeline Portal · RFP-Admin role. Canonical automation surface is /admin/workflows; /admin/process (event monitor) and /admin/processes (instance ledger) are legacy views of the same runs. Companion guides: Customer-Admin, Collaborator.

sections.heading: Sign in & the admin landing
body: Sign in as your RFP-admin account. The landing is role-aware: it opens the operations console with your live ToDos — purchases awaiting curation, RFPs mid-triage, and workflows parked on a human gate.

The seeded operator eric@rfppipeline.com is a master_admin: global access to every tenant plus the full admin surface. No per-tenant grant needed — it can dip into any company and rise back up to ingest.
sections.caption: The admin operations landing with role-aware ToDos.

sections.heading: Setup — source monitoring & scouts
body: Before anything is ingested, point the platform at where opportunities live. Sources defines the sites and feeds to watch; Scouts is the worker pool that visits them on a schedule, diffs the results, and surfaces new or changed solicitations. Configure regions to watch, run a scout on demand, and review the diffs.
sections.caption: Source monitoring profiles — the watched feeds that scouts sweep.

sections.heading: The scout worker pool
sections.body: The scout pool shows each worker, its schedule, last run, and yield. Scouts run managed and audited — a run that fails on one source continues on the others. Newly discovered solicitations land in the intake queue for triage.
sections.caption: The scout worker pool — scheduled discovery across all sources.

sections.heading: Ingest — upload an RFP
body: To bring a solicitation in by hand, use Upload. Drop the solicitation PDF(s); the ingestor extracts text (with an ingest-assist pass), de-duplicates against existing solicitations, and stages the documents in object storage. It handles multi-document packages and marks a primary.
Malformed source PDFs (odd fonts, embedded control characters) are sanitized on the way in — the atomizer and ingestor strip invalid bytes so a bad file can't poison downstream text.
sections.caption: Uploading a solicitation package into curation.

sections.heading: Curate — triage, topics, compliance, skeleton
body: Curation is the heart of the operator's work. Open a solicitation to triage it, extract its topics (umbrella + every sub-topic), attach the compliance requirements (from a preset or suggested), and build the section skeleton that becomes each proposal's matrix. Apply a preset to one topic or fan it to all.
Verified on DON26BX03-NP002: triaged, topics extracted, the DON 6-volume CSO compliance attached, and the Technical Volume 2 skeleton linked to its template mold.
sections.caption: The curation workspace — triage, topics, compliance, and skeleton.

sections.heading: Templates & molds studio
body: The Template Studio is where section molds live — the format contracts (page limit, margins, font, required structure) a required item points at. Author a template on the canvas, or templify a winning past proposal into a reusable skeleton, then attach it to a compliance item so every provisioned proposal inherits the right shape.
sections.caption: The Template Studio — section molds and templified skeletons.

sections.heading: Push opportunities to customers
body: When a solicitation is curated, push it. The push fans every activated opportunity (umbrella + all topics) across the forward-only opportunity bridge into a denormalized card for every tenant, auto-scored against each tenant's buckets on arrival. This is the discovery release — customers now see the opportunity ranked in their pipeline.
Verified: the C-UAS topic pushed to Immobileyes ranked #1 in their pipeline within the same run.
sections.caption: Activated opportunities — the push fans them onto every tenant's cards.

sections.heading: Purchases & the curation release (72h SLA)
body: When a customer buys a proposal portal with a comp code, it lands in Purchases as curation_pending with a 72-hour SLA. You release it from the shadow account: releasing provisions the build unlocked and instantiates the compliance matrix + molds from the master solicitation. This is the second release over the bridge — the proposal-portal build.
sections.caption: The purchase queue — comp-code buys awaiting curation release.

sections.heading: Monitor — the workflow catalog & instances
body: Every automation runs as a managed workflow — no fire-and-forget. Workflows is the canonical control surface: the roster of templates with an activation toggle, plus live instances with a per-step progress bar, transition timeline, and outcomes. A step that fails continues on independent branches; a human gate (HITL / ToDo) parks the instance until you advance it.
From an instance you can advance, retry, or cancel. A paused instance shows exactly which gate it's waiting on and who it's assigned to.
sections.caption: The workflow catalog + live instances — see and control every automation.

sections.heading: Monitor — the agent workforce
body: Agents is the workforce roster: each archetype, whether it's awake, and its per-tenant usage over the forward-only bridge. Tenant-space agents are tenant-bound and advisory — they propose, a guardrail checks, and a human accepts; they never auto-write business tables. Guardrail defaults sets the safety envelope (round/cost/rate/budget caps) every agent runs inside.
sections.caption: The agent workforce roster with per-tenant usage.

sections.heading: Monitor — events, automation, processes
body: Cross-board observability: Events is the immutable stream (every state-changing action emits start→end); Automation is the rules engine with its run logs; Process / Processes are event-based monitors of active instances. Use these to answer “what happened, when, and did it finish?” for any run on either side of the bridge.
Naming overlap to know: /admin/process (event monitor), /admin/processes (instance ledger), and /admin/workflows (canonical) view the same runs. Treat /admin/workflows as primary.
sections.caption: The automation rules engine and its run logs.

sections.heading: Monitor — system state & analytics
sections.body: System state is the health board (services, storage, migrations); Analytics rolls up usage across tenants and opportunities. Together they tell you the platform is healthy and where the activity is.
sections.caption: The system-state health board.

sections.heading: Tenants oversight & shadow-descend
body: Tenants is the roster of every company on the platform. From a tenant you can review its state, backfill its cards, and — the operator's superpower — shadow-descend into its portal to do work on its behalf (build a library, draft a section, unstick a proposal), then rise back up to the admin surface to ingest more. The session rewrites to tenant_admin inside the portal and a shadow banner marks the descent; every action stays audited.
Verified: eric@rfppipeline.com descends into /portal/immobileyes/* (shadow banner shown), works the proposal, and returns to /admin. One account, both jobs.
sections.caption: Shadow-descend: the RFP admin working inside the Immobileyes portal, banner shown.
